text: This humanoid has twenty nine joints, a free base, and per link masses and inertias.
Both robots receive the same reaching commands and synthetic delays. The simulation includes gravity, floor contact, joint torque limits, and body inertia.
On the left, joint groups apply commands as they arrive. Delayed leg updates can leave the arms and legs working on different command versions.
On the right, the supervisor waits for a complete whole body command. This preserves coordination, but makes the robot wait for the slowest group.
Across eight matched seeds, synchronization reduced peak body tilt. Both robots stayed upright and reached the target.
This is an exploratory standing and reaching test, not a trained laundry robot. Clothing, door manipulation, and hardware validation still remain.
